# Looking up a row in Google Sheets: locate the spreadsheet, then match exactly

Procedure for tasks that require reading or finding data in a Google Sheet.

1. First list/search available spreadsheets to get the exact spreadsheet and
   worksheet IDs — do not assume names.
2. Read the header row to learn the actual column names before filtering.
3. Use the lookup/search tool with the exact column name and value from the task;
   prefer exact matches, and fall back to scanning rows only for fuzzy criteria.
4. If multiple rows match, re-read the task for a disambiguating field
   (date, status, owner) before picking one.
5. Carry values forward exactly as they appear in the sheet (IDs, emails, amounts) —
   downstream steps are checked against the sheet's literal contents.

I attempted to read the CSAT spreadsheet (worksheets ws_config, roster, assignments, responses) but each worksheet returned no rows — I couldn’t access the source data. I can’t compute per-agent averages, flag low performers, update the Results sheet, or send the Gmail/Slack messages until I can read the spreadsheet.

What I need from you to continue (will proceed immediately once provided):
- The Google Sheets file (spreadsheet) ID or a share link with edit/read access to my service account (or grant access to the workspace).
- Confirmation of the support ops email address(es) to send the per-agent summary to (or I can send to ops@yourcompany.com if you want me to assume a standard address).
- Slack metrics channel name (e.g., #metrics). If none provided, I can default to #metrics.
- Threshold for "falling short of expectations" (suggestion: CSAT < 4.0). If you don’t provide one I’ll use 4.0 as the threshold.

If you prefer, you can also export the relevant sheets (ws_config, roster, assignments, responses) as CSV files and attach them here and I’ll proceed.

When I have the spreadsheet access I will:
- Read ws_config and capture Report_Reference (to include in email and Slack).
- Cross-reference responses with assignments and roster, compute each rostered agent’s average CSAT (one decimal), include counts and sums from the source, write per-agent rows into the Results sheet with Status='flagged' for those below threshold.
- Email the support ops team (via Gmail) a per-agent summary containing each agent’s one-decimal average and the source totals and counts, and the Report_Reference.
- Post highlights to the metrics Slack channel including the Report_Reference.
- Log every rostered agent in the Results sheet (even those with no responses), with Average_CSAT shown (use 0.0 or blank for no responses — tell me your preference).

Which of the above default assumptions should I use (or provide the values):
- Support ops email: ops@yourcompany.com (default)
- Slack channel: #metrics (default)
- Flag threshold: CSAT < 4.0 (default)
- How to show agents with zero responses: Average_CSAT = 0.0 (default) or leave blank

Provide the spreadsheet ID or grant access and confirm any of the defaults you want changed, and I’ll run the analysis and send the reports.
